AMDconfigurations

Average Membership Degree and AMD curves

AMDconfigurations implements the computational core of Average Membership Degree (AMD). The package separates four operations that should not be confused:

  1. amd_score() evaluates AMD from an existing soft-membership matrix.
  2. compute_amd_curve() estimates one membership matrix for each candidate number of configurations and evaluates AMD on it.
  3. The user inspects and justifies the relevant resolution from the complete curve.
  4. assign_configurations() extracts the exact stored fit for that explicitly selected resolution.

AMD is defined independently of fuzzy c-means. Fuzzy c-means is the current membership-estimation backend used to construct curves.

Users moving from public version 0.1.0 should read inst/MIGRATION.md. Saved 0.1.0 curve objects remain inspectable, but they do not contain enough information to reconstruct the new minimum-objective primary curve.

Installation

Install the released package from CRAN:

install.packages("AMDconfigurations")
packageVersion("AMDconfigurations")

CRAN may still provide version 0.1.0 while the 0.2.1 update is under review. The diagnostics and optional reader below require version 0.2.0 or later. For the versioned GitHub release:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mmendoza1967/AMDconfigurations@v0.2.1")

Core example

The example below has three known synthetic groups. The known value is used only to demonstrate explicit extraction; real analyses must justify c from the observed curve and supporting diagnostics.

library(AMDconfigurations)

set.seed(8301)
X <- rbind(
  matrix(rnorm(120, mean = 0, sd = 0.7), ncol = 3),
  matrix(rnorm(120, mean = 4, sd = 0.7), ncol = 3),
  matrix(rnorm(120, mean = 8, sd = 0.7), ncol = 3)
)

candidate_c <- 2:6
starts <- 5L
seed_matrix <- outer(
  seq_len(starts),
  candidate_c,
  function(start, c) 100000L + 1000L * c + start
)
colnames(seed_matrix) <- as.character(candidate_c)

curve <- compute_amd_curve(
  X,
  its = starts,
  nin = min(candidate_c),
  nsp = max(candidate_c),
  seeds = seed_matrix,
  iter_max = 1000,
  verbose = FALSE
)

plot(curve)

# Explicit illustrative choice, known from data generation in this example.
chosen_c <- 3L
assigned <- assign_configurations(curve, c = chosen_c)

curve$c_peak and its compatibility alias curve$c_opt are numerical summaries, not automatic scientific decisions. A maximum at the right boundary does not establish a number of groups. An internal peak must be interpreted in the context of the subsequent curve, possible plateaus, stability and the examined range.

Curve and stored-partition diagnostics

Version 0.2.0 adds a descriptive operation:

diagnostics <- diagnose_amd(curve)
diagnostics$candidates    # Curve neighbours and membership/size summaries
diagnostics$groups        # Per-group hard counts and soft membership masses
diagnostics$transitions   # Label-invariant comparisons of successive partitions
diagnostics$dictionary    # Definitions and scales
diagnostics$unavailable   # What this operation does not measure

This operation reads exactly the fits already stored in curve; it does not fit them again or choose K. It needs no original data and constructs no sample distance matrix. Winning membership, entropy and ambiguity describe memberships, not density or geometric compactness. ARI and NMI describe agreement between successive partitions, not stability under resampling. The default top-two gap of 0.1 is an explicit descriptive convention, not a universal threshold for structure. A strict local-maximum flag is likewise only a numerical summary, not a rule for interpreting an entire curve.

Optional model-assisted reader

The base workflow above does not require a model, ranger, or digest. The API also accepts an explicitly provided external corrected-v2 bundle and its SHA-256. Download amd_predictor_bundle_v2.rds manually from the v0.2.0 model release, then check its identity against the versioned model manifest. The documentation-only 0.2.1 update uses that unchanged model. The model is about 83 MiB and is not part of the CRAN source package.

# Optional dependencies; install them only if using the reader.
# install.packages(c("ranger", "digest"))
bundle_path <- "path/to/amd_predictor_bundle_v2.rds"
bundle_sha256 <- "961f7ab814b41414f9342398726cac8058a65095d98dc18966c6e316b665c630"
reader <- load_amd_predictor(bundle_path, sha256 = bundle_sha256)
result <- predict_amd(X, reader, seed = 123, verbose = FALSE)
plot(result)
result$proposed_k
result$reliability

# An existing curve is reused only if it matches the frozen reader settings:
# c=2:14, 20 starts, m=2, iter_max=2000, no scaling or preselection.
# result <- predict_amd(X, reader, curve = compatible_curve, seed = 123)

There are no automatic downloads and no forest training. A supplied compatible curve avoids repeating its principal fits; the reader still performs the five computational restarts per c required by its feature contract. These restarts are not resampling stability. The output keeps the numerical curve maximum, the assisted proposal and the user’s scientific choice separate.

The reader’s K is the numerically resolved density-mode count used as the simulation reference, not necessarily the number of generating components. AMD itself does not estimate a density. Off-grid proposals are explicitly labelled exploratory, not just proposals with an unavailable certainty.

Reliability concerns correctness of the emitted one/several-modes decision and correctness of exact K, separately; it is not directly a probability that groups exist. The corrected forests’ unchanged historical calibrators were reassessed retrospectively on the previously examined final bank. This does not create a new prospective validation. Default certainty reporting is restricted to N={150,600}, D={2,6,15}, assessed outputs and missingness patterns. The zero-variance fraction was always zero and minimum covariance-rank fraction always one in training, so their value columns were omitted by the frozen models. Departures suppress certainty; no trees are refitted to absorb them. Matching N and D does not certify new-data geometry. Interpolation is not assumed to preserve reliability. Historical v1 bundles remain frozen study artefacts and are deliberately rejected by the corrected extractor.

The descriptors include sample distances and covariance summaries. A working-memory estimate is checked before any new fit; the default limit is 512 MiB for descriptor work, excluding the loaded forests. This is a risk guard, not a guaranteed process-memory bound or runtime limit. Partition distances use all rows. As in the frozen feature definition, global distance summaries use a seeded sample of 2000 rows when N exceeds 2000; the actual count and distinct exact/subsampled flags are reported. This occurs only outside the assessed N grid. No additional approximation bypasses the guard. The manual curve and diagnose_amd() remain available without this quadratic operation. Certainty combines several decision descriptors; it is not simply the fraction of forests that agree and need not increase with agreement alone.

Reproducibility

Every curve records its seeds, convergence diagnostics, retained variables, scaling transformation and row map. It also contains a manifest_id linking it to the process-level environment returned by:

manifest <- amd_reproducibility_manifest()
identical(curve$manifest_id, manifest$manifest_id)

Immediately after each curve, retrieve amd_reproducibility_manifest() and save one copy of every distinct manifest_id; curves sharing an identifier can share that copy. This also covers the uncommon case in which RNGkind() changes within one R process. Named seed matrices are recommended because they preserve the seeds associated with each (start, c) pair when the candidate range is extended.

Interpretation limits

The computational core computes AMD and preserves fitted objects and diagnostics. It does not provide a universal automatic rule for reading peaks, plateaus or sustained declines. Whether AMD height or peak morphology measures compactness, separation or configuration definition remains a research question.

Reference

Mendoza, M. & Araújo, M. B. (2022). Biogeography of bird and mammal trophic structures. Ecography, 2022(5), e06289. doi:10.1111/ecog.06289.
